title: The First Black Woman in Space: Mae Jemison's Amazing Journey
summary:
Imagine floating in space, looking down at Earth. On September 12, 1992, Mae Jemison did exactly that — and made history. She became the first African American woman to go to space. Have you ever dreamed of being an astronaut? Jemison proved that dream is possible for everyone.

Jemison wasn't just an astronaut. She was also a medical doctor and an engineer. Before joining NASA, she worked as a doctor in West Africa for the Peace Corps. She helped people in Sierra Leone and Liberia. Then she applied to become an astronaut. NASA chose her in 1987.

On her mission, she flew on the space shuttle Endeavour. She spent 8 days in orbit. That's 190 hours in space! She ran 44 different science experiments. She studied how bones work in space. She also did experiments for Japan and the United States.

Jemison was inspired by a TV show. She watched Star Trek and saw Lt. Uhura, a Black woman in space. That showed her that she could do it too. Later, in 1993, Jemison appeared on Star Trek: The Next Generation. Her dream came full circle.

Why does this matter? Jemison showed that space is for everyone. In NASA's early days, women and people of color were not chosen. NASA didn't send a woman to space until 1983. The first Black man went in 1983 too. But the first Black woman had to wait until 1992. Jemison's flight was a big step forward. She retired from NASA in 1993 and started her own company. She continues to inspire kids to reach for the stars.
why_it_matters: Jemison's journey shows kids that even a dream as far away as space can be open to them if they keep learning and working for it.

background_read: NASA is the United States space agency. It picked its first astronauts in the 1950s and 1960s, and they were all white men, so it took many years before women and people of color could join.

Star Trek is a famous science-fiction TV show about people exploring space. Lt. Uhura, played by Nichelle Nichols, was one of the first Black women shown on American TV with an important professional job.
The space shuttle Endeavour was a reusable spacecraft. NASA used space shuttles for many years to carry astronauts and cargo into orbit and then land them back on Earth.
